headline_marked: [[Iran launches missile & drone attacks]] on US military sites in Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain
headline: Iran launches missile & drone attacks on US military sites in Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, Bahrain
summary: Iran's IRGC claims missile and drone attacks on US military positions across four countries, alleging drone destruction and US casualties. However, the US and Jordan deny any significant damage or fatalities from these strikes.
details: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) announced missile and drone attacks on US military positions in Jordan, Iraq, Kuwait, and Bahrain on Tuesday night. This action was stated to be in retaliation for earlier US attacks in southern Iran.

The IRGC specifically claimed a "heavy" ballistic missile attack on hangars housing RQ-4 and MQ-9 drones at Jordan's Prince Hassan Air Base. They reported several drones were destroyed, multiple US flight and technical personnel were killed, and technical infrastructure caught fire.

However, both the United States and Jordan have denied any casualties or significant damage from these attacks. A US source, speaking to Al-Jazeera, confirmed that US forces successfully repelled the attack on Camp Titen in Jordan.

Jordan's military reported that its air defense system intercepted 10 out of 13 ballistic missiles launched from Iranian territory. The remaining three landed in remote areas away from populated zones, causing no casualties or damage.

The IRGC also claimed coordinated missile and drone attacks on US facilities in Erbil province, northern Iraq. They alleged the destruction of a repair center, a technical equipment warehouse, and a US surveillance balloon guidance system, along with fires in fuel tanks and several US casualties.

Kuwait's army stated its air defense system repelled "enemy drone" attacks, attributing explosions heard to drones being shot down. Iran's Tasnim news agency, citing the army, reported drones targeting US-deployed areas and radar facilities at Bahrain's Sheikh Isa Air Base.

The IRGC stated these retaliatory strikes were in response to a US attack on a wedding ceremony in Sirik, Hormozgan province. They claim that attack killed four people, including a child, and severely injured several others.

These exchanges mark the first direct retaliatory attacks between the two countries since July. Earlier on Tuesday, the US conducted airstrikes in several areas of southern Iran, including Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, and Chabahar.

US President Donald Trump had previously warned of "severe" strikes against Tehran if Iran retaliated. He reiterated this warning, stating that any further Iranian counter-attacks would be met with even harsher US responses.

headline_marked: [[New syndicate strategy for Malaysia jobs]] could hike costs to BDT 6-7 lakh
headline: New syndicate strategy for Malaysia jobs could hike costs to BDT 6-7 lakh
summary: A new syndicate, allegedly involving familiar players, is using a different strategy for sending workers to Malaysia, potentially increasing costs significantly. Many of the 25 selected agencies lack prior experience.
details: A new syndicate is reportedly operating with a different strategy for sending Bangladeshi workers to Malaysia, potentially driving up costs to BDT 6-7 lakh per worker. This is significantly higher than the previous average of BDT 5.44 lakh.
Out of 25 agencies selected to send workers to Malaysia, 17 have no prior experience in this sector. Only 8 agencies collectively sent 1,612 workers, with five sending fewer than 202 each.

The selection process, which lacked specific criteria from Malaysia, is allegedly controlled by Bestinet, owner of the MyEG system. Bestinet is owned by Bangladeshi-origin Malaysian citizen Aminul Islam bin Abdul Noor, known as Amin Noor.

Amin Noor is accused of controlling the entire worker recruitment trade from Malaysia. His alleged representative in Bangladesh is Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, former Secretary-General of BAIRA, who is now in hiding abroad.

Swapan's agency license has been revoked, and he faces ongoing cases and an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) investigation. The ACC recently requested information on 57 agencies, including three of the newly selected ones, for alleged involvement in human trafficking and illegal wealth.

State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment, Md. Nurul Haq, stated that an interim government list of 423 agencies was sent to Malaysia, which then selected 25. Malaysia also added 338 assisting agencies.

The Minister affirmed that the ministry would set a cost limit to ensure lower expenses for workers. He also stated that any agency accused of trafficking or corruption found on the list would be reported to Malaysia, and their licenses would be revoked.

Among the 17 inexperienced agencies are Tania Trade, Satkhira International, A-Plus, Al Hayat Overseas, Valley Trade, Khan Jahan Ali Overseas, Bengal Human Resource, Earth Smart, At Takwa, Motherland, Mangrove, Jewel Rinku Enterprise, Bangladesh One Overseas, Anwesha Air, Chandpur International, Goodness Services, and Valuka Overseas.
